ui.cors.intro: Tests the CORS policy with four different origin patterns.
ui.jwt.intro: Analyzes a JWT and detects issues such as alg:none, kid injection and a missing exp claim.
ui.ssl.intro: Reviews the TLS version, cipher suite, certificate expiry and hostname match.
ui.ssl.subject: Subject
ui.cookie.intro: Checks the Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite flags and assesses session fixation, CSRF and XSS risk.
api.error.invalid_url: That does not look like a valid URL.
api.error.unsupported_scheme: Only http and https URLs can be scanned.
api.error.blocked_address: Scanning private or internal addresses ({{ip}}) is not allowed.
api.error.validation_failed: Could not validate the scan target: {{reason}}
api.error.rate_limited: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
analyzer.header.hsts.desc: Tells the browser to always use HTTPS. An important header for preventing man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.
analyzer.header.hsts.advice.missing: Add the HSTS header and set max-age to at least 31536000 (one year).
analyzer.header.hsts.advice.max_age_zero: max-age=0 disables HSTS. Set a sensible value, for example max-age=31536000.
analyzer.header.hsts.advice.no_preload: Adding the preload directive makes this safer.
analyzer.header.hsts.advice.no_subdomain: Consider adding the includeSubDomains and preload directives.
analyzer.header.csp.desc: A powerful header for preventing cross-site scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
analyzer.header.csp.advice.missing: Set a CSP header. Starting with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' is a good first step.
analyzer.header.csp.advice.unsafe_inline: unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval are dangerous. Consider moving to a nonce- or hash-based CSP.
The policy contains unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval. Consider a stricter policy.
analyzer.header.x_frame_options.desc: Prevents clickjacking by controlling whether the page can be embedded in an iframe.
analyzer.header.x_frame_options.advice.m: Set X-Frame-Options to DENY or SAMEORIGIN.
analyzer.header.x_content_type_options.d: Stops the browser from MIME-sniffing the response content type.
analyzer.header.referrer_policy.desc: Controls how much referrer information is sent, which protects user privacy.
analyzer.header.referrer_policy.advice.w: Use a stricter policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
analyzer.header.permissions_policy.desc: Controls access to browser APIs such as the camera, microphone and geolocation.
analyzer.header.permissions_policy.advic: Set a Permissions-Policy to restrict access to browser features you do not need.
analyzer.header.x_xss_protection.desc: An XSS filter setting for older browsers. Modern browsers rely on CSP instead.
Set X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block for legacy browsers.
analyzer.header.cache_control.desc: Controls caching of confidential pages so that sensitive information is not left behind.
analyzer.header.cache_control.advice.mis: Set Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache on pages that hold sensitive data.
analyzer.header.cache_control.advice.wea: For pages that hold sensitive data, use no-store, no-cache.
analyzer.cors.test.origin_reflection.des: If an attacker's origin is reflected verbatim in the ACAO header, credentials can be stolen through cross-origin requests.
analyzer.cors.test.null_origin.name: Null origin bypass
analyzer.cors.test.null_origin.desc: A null origin can be sent from a sandboxed iframe, so trusting null lets an attacker abuse it.
analyzer.cors.test.pre_domain.name: Prefix domain match
analyzer.cors.test.pre_domain.desc: If origins are validated by prefix matching, a spoofed domain such as evil-victim.com is allowed.
analyzer.cors.test.post_domain.name: Suffix domain match
analyzer.cors.test.post_domain.desc: If origins are validated by suffix matching, a spoofed domain such as victim.com.evil.com is allowed.
analyzer.jwt.parse_error.invalid_parts: A JWT must consist of three parts (header.payload.signature)
analyzer.jwt.finding.alg_none.title: alg: none — no signature verification
analyzer.jwt.finding.alg_none.desc: alg=none skips JWT signature verification, so an attacker can tamper with the payload at will (equivalent to CVE-2015-9235).
analyzer.jwt.finding.alg_symmetric.title: Symmetric algorithm in use: {{alg}}
analyzer.jwt.finding.alg_symmetric.desc: HMAC algorithms depend on the strength of the shared secret, and weak keys are open to brute force. Consider moving to RS256 or ES256.
analyzer.jwt.finding.alg_asymmetric.desc: Public-key cryptography is in use. Watch out for algorithm confusion attacks (RS256 to HS256).
analyzer.jwt.finding.kid_injection.title: Possible kid injection
analyzer.jwt.finding.kid_injection.desc: The kid field contains a suspicious string: "{{kid}}". SQL injection or path traversal may be possible.
analyzer.jwt.finding.token_expired.title: Token has expired
analyzer.jwt.finding.token_expired.desc: The exp claim is in the past ({{expires_at}}). Accepting expired tokens is a security risk.
analyzer.jwt.finding.long_expiry.title: Expiry is too far out
analyzer.jwt.finding.long_expiry.desc: The token is valid for more than 30 days ({{expires_at}}). A shorter lifetime is recommended.
analyzer.jwt.finding.no_exp.title: No exp claim
analyzer.jwt.finding.no_exp.desc: No expiry (exp) is set, so the token stays valid forever and the impact of a leak is much larger.
analyzer.jwt.finding.nbf_future.title: nbf is in the future
analyzer.jwt.finding.nbf_future.desc: nbf (Not Before) is in the future ({{not_before}}), so this token is not valid yet.
analyzer.jwt.finding.sensitive_claim.des: A JWT payload is only Base64-encoded, not encrypted. Do not put sensitive data in it.
analyzer.jwt.finding.no_issues.title: No obvious problems were found
analyzer.jwt.finding.no_issues.desc: Static analysis found nothing. Verify the signature itself on the server side.
analyzer.ssl.finding.legacy_tls.title: Outdated TLS version in use: {{version}}
analyzer.ssl.finding.legacy_tls.desc: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 were deprecated by RFC 8996 in 2020. Move to TLS 1.2 or later.
analyzer.ssl.finding.tls12.title: TLS 1.2 in use
analyzer.ssl.finding.tls12.desc: TLS 1.2 is still safe, but moving to TLS 1.3 improves both security and performance.
analyzer.ssl.finding.tls13.title: TLS 1.3 ✓ latest version in use
analyzer.ssl.finding.tls13.desc: TLS 1.3 is the newest and most secure version of TLS.
analyzer.ssl.finding.weak_cipher.title: Weak cipher suite: {{cipher}}
analyzer.ssl.finding.weak_cipher.desc: Disable weak cipher suites such as RC4, DES, 3DES and EXPORT.
analyzer.ssl.finding.self_signed.title: Self-signed certificate
analyzer.ssl.finding.self_signed.desc: The certificate was not issued by a trusted certificate authority. Do not use it in production.
analyzer.ssl.finding.cert_expired.title: Certificate has expired
analyzer.ssl.finding.cert_expired.desc_o: The certificate expired {{count}} day ago. Browsers will block the connection.
The certificate expired {{count}} days ago. Browsers will block the connection.
analyzer.ssl.finding.cert_expiring_criti: Renewing the certificate is urgent. Renew it now, for example with Let's Encrypt.
The certificate expires within 30 days. Renew it soon.
analyzer.ssl.finding.cert_expiring_warni: The certificate expires within 60 days. Start preparing to renew it.
analyzer.ssl.finding.hostname_mismatch.d: The certificate CN/SAN does not match the hostname "{{host}}". This may be phishing or a misconfiguration.
analyzer.ssl.finding.rsa_key.title: RSA public key
analyzer.ssl.finding.rsa_key.desc: Use RSA keys of 2048 bits or more. Moving to ECDSA also improves performance.
analyzer.ssl.finding.ecdsa_key.title: ECDSA public key ✓
analyzer.ssl.finding.ecdsa_key.desc: ECDSA is an efficient and secure public-key algorithm.
analyzer.ssl.finding.legacy_accepted.des: {{protocol}} is a deprecated protocol. Disable it in your server configuration.
analyzer.cookie.issue.no_secure: No Secure flag — the cookie may be sent over plain HTTP
analyzer.cookie.issue.no_http_only: No HttpOnly flag — readable from JavaScript through document.cookie
analyzer.cookie.issue.no_http_only_sensi: No HttpOnly flag — readable from JavaScript through document.cookie (sensitive cookie)
analyzer.cookie.issue.same_site_none: SameSite=None — the cookie is sent on cross-site requests
analyzer.cookie.issue.same_site_none_sen: No SameSite=Strict/Lax — may be open to CSRF (sensitive cookie)
analyzer.cookie.issue.same_site_unset: No SameSite attribute — the cookie is sent on cross-site requests
analyzer.cookie.issue.same_site_unset_se: No SameSite attribute — may be open to CSRF (sensitive cookie)
